title: A finitely generated ideal inside the radical of another has a power inside it
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I,J\subseteq A$ ideals with $I$ finitely generated and $I\subseteq\sqrt J=\{x\in A:x^m\in J\text{ for some }m\ge1\}$. Then there is an integer $t\ge1$ with $I^t\subseteq J$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00IM (lemma-Noetherian-power, line 6300), whose proof (J=(f_1,...,f_s), f_i^{d_i} in I, n = d_1+...+d_s+1) uses only that the ideal is finitely generated; used without reference in the proof of Lemma Tag 0394 (lemma-finite-after-completion, line 23120: "the fact that n is finitely generated implies that n^t is contained in mS")

mathlib_searches.query: finitely generated ideal contained in radical of J has a power contained in J
if I is finitely generated and I ⊆ radical J then I^n ⊆ J for some n

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: (h' : I ≤ J.radical) (h : I.FG) : ∃ n, I ^ n ≤ J, for a commutative semiring; if the n obtained is 0 then J = A and t = 1 works (I^1 ≤ I^0 = ⊤ = J). Source read 2026-10-10
